label: Person
name: Agustín Pipia
summary:
Agustín Pipia (1661–1730) was an Italian Dominican cardinal and theologian who served as Master General of the Dominican Order before his elevation to the cardinalate. Born in Savona in Liguria, he joined the Dominicans and rose through their academic and governance structures to lead the entire order as Master General from 1721 to 1725.

Pipia's tenure as Dominican Master General came at a significant moment for the order: the eighteenth century saw the Dominicans navigating the challenges of Enlightenment rationalism, Jansenist controversy, and the decline of scholastic theology's dominance in Catholic intellectual culture. As Master General, he oversaw the order's global operations—including missions in the Americas, Asia, and Africa—and maintained its intellectual and spiritual traditions.

His elevation to the cardinalate by Pope Benedict XIII in 1725 crowned his career and gave him a role in the central governance of the universal Church. His Dominican formation and leadership made him a significant representative of the mendicant tradition within the Roman Curia. He died in 1730, having guided one of Catholicism's most intellectually distinguished orders through a period of significant cultural challenge.
